CHAPTER V
FORMS OF VIOLENCE AND PROTECTION
Article 6
(1) Forms of violence against Women and Children include physical, sexual, economic and psychological.
(2) Forms of physical violence are any acts that result in pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, loss of consciousness and/or cause death.
(3) Forms of sexual violence are sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or specific purposes.
(4) Forms of economic violence are neglect of family members in the form of not providing livelihood, care or maintenance as appropriate.
(5) Forms of psychological violence are acts that result in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering in a person.
1.2.rationale: The policy explicitly lists sexual violence as a form of violence against women and children and defines it.

Article 8
(1) Forms of protection for Women and Child Victims of Violence include medical, legal, medicolegal (forensic medicine), economic and psychological protection.
(2) The form of medical protection for Women and Child Victims of Violence as referred to in paragraph (1) is in the form of treatment and recovery of physical injuries aimed at restoring the physical condition of victims carried out by medical personnel and paramedics free of charge.
(3) The form of legal protection for Women and Child Victims of Violence as referred to in paragraph (1) is in the form of services and assistance to help victims undergo legal and judicial processes.
(4) The form of medicolegal protection for Women and Child Victims of Violence as referred to in paragraph (1) is in the form of medical services for evidentiary purposes in the legal field.
(5) The form of economic protection for Women and Child Victims of Violence as referred to in paragraph (1) is in the form of services for skills and providing economic access so that victims can be independent.
(6) The form of psychological protection for Women and Child Victims of Violence as referred to in paragraph (1) is in the form of assistance in order to restore the traumatic condition of victims including the provision of safe houses to protect victims from various threats and intimidation for victims and providing psychological support so that victims have self-confidence, strength and independence in resolving problems.
3.4.rationale: The policy includes psychological protection that encompasses provision of safe houses to protect victims from threats and intimidation, indicating shelter services.
